fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Perimeter Fencing; Access Drive; Open Green Space
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Multiple Structures; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Fenced Sections
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responding units can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the access drive entrance clearly so crews arriving at night or under low-visibility conditions can distinguish it from adjacent driveways or openings.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so fire apparatus and emergency units can reach both structures without delay.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive that narrows the travel lane or reduces overhead clearance for larger emergency vehicles.
• Install a reflective or clearly labeled marker at the detached structure to help crews identify it as a separate building requiring independent size-up.
• Keep a gate or opening in the perimeter fencing accessible from the front, so crews do not have to breach fencing to reach the rear of the property.
• If rear fencing sections are locked, install a Knox-compatible lock or post a visible key box so crews can open them without forcing entry.
• Thin dense vegetation between the main residence and the detached structure so crews can move between buildings without obstruction.
• Keep the walkway between structures clear of stored items, equipment, or overgrowth so responders can move quickly on foot.
• Identify and communicate to your local fire station that the property has a single vehicle access point, so crews can plan for limited turnaround space before arriving.
• Maintain a clear staging area near the front

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Open Green Space; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Shrubs; Mixed Vegetation; Long Driveway; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Scattered Trees; Ground Vegetation; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly against or within a few feet of the house.
• Thin scattered shrubs across the property to reduce connected patches of vegetation between trees and structures.
• Remove or cut back ground vegetation growing close to the base of the house.
• Separate mixed vegetation groupings near the structure so individual plants and shrubs are not touching each other.
• Keep low-hanging tree branches trimmed up from the ground to reduce the path fire can travel from ground vegetation into the tree canopy.
• Clear any overhanging branches above the driveway to maintain safe passage for vehicles along its full length.
• Keep the driveway surface and edges free of accumulated dead leaves, twigs, and loose plant material.
• Mark or keep clear a turning area near the structure to allow emergency vehicles to reverse out without entering the limited rear access area.
• Maintain the open green space areas by mowing or cutting ground vegetation regularly to keep it short.
• Avoid storing wood, debris, or other flammable materials against or near the structure where scattered shrubs or ground vegetation are also present.
